title: Activate project card: receipts read plus one button that drives the chain
description:
SPIDR child C of task-bb844c288fb346c0856778c738b9f073. dependsOn child B (task-4b9c394debe94b41a80e2b46c6d55ab8). Filed by architect-d1711c47 2026-09-04, measured at main 68eb1c5d.

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: (1) a daemon read that STATES each receipt as measured/missing with its reason, so the card can render before anything is clicked; (2) the v2 'Activate project' card that lists those receipts and drives register -> bind_repository -> provider.probe -> project.activate from one button.

MEASURED AT 68eb1c5d:
- COPY THIS PATTERN: apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/policy-install-port.ts (83 lines) already does exactly this shape for policy - `readSurfaceOnce` POSTs /affordances/read, `installStandardPolicy` loops the slices, RE-READS the surface between steps because each commit moves the aggregate version, finds the offer by commandKind, spends it via `spendOffer`, and STOPS AT THE FIRST REFUSAL keeping the daemon's own code+layer. Its consumer is apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/live-ops.tsx:95. Mirror it; do not invent a second dispatch idiom.
- The offer/refusal wire is apps/control-room/src/v2/approvals/offer-wire.ts (`spendOffer`, OfferOutcome) and apps/control-room/src/live/live-board-feed.ts (`frameOfSurface`, SurfaceFrame with .offers/.steps/.outcome/.connection).
- apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts is ALREADY 422 lines - over the 400 hard cap. DO NOT ADD TO IT. Add a separate route module alongside apps/daemon/src/http/policy-read.ts and runs-read.ts, which is the shipped idiom for a dedicated read.
- apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener.ts registers routes; a new read route is the 8-touchpoint + .js bridge pattern and needs its roster/roster-test backfill (bidirectional set-equality, global rail 9).
- The chain's four kinds and their prerequisite order are at apps/daemon/src/bootstrap/bootstrap-sequence.ts:31/:107; apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/work-labels.ts:46 already maps "project.activate" -> "Activate the project", so the card's labels come from there, not from new strings.

DESIGN (settled, do not re-derive): the card NEVER spells a witness - child B made the daemon mint it, so the card sends `project.activate` and shows the answer. Receipts render measured/missing with the DAEMON'S reason text verbatim, never a paraphrase, and never a credential value. The button drives the four commands SEQUENTIALLY, re-reading the surface between each (versions move), stopping at the first refusal with the daemon's code @ layer shown.

NOT IN SCOPE: the live-goal-create.ts copy replacement, the Playwright journey, README/runbook (all child D). Do not touch tests/e2e.
definitionOfDone: A dedicated daemon read module under apps/daemon/src/http/ (NOT affordance-read.ts, which is already 422 lines) answers with each of the six receipts as measured/missing plus its reason, sourced from child A's measurement surface; a test asserts a missing member is reported with its stable code and that no credential VALUE and no secret appears anywhere in the response body.

The route is registered in http-listener.ts and carries its .js bridge; the read-route roster and its asserting test are updated with BIDIRECTIONAL set-equality - enumerate the served set from the dispatch/route seam, not only from the roster constant (global rail 9), so deleting a route cannot stay green.

apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/ gains an activation port mirroring policy-install-port.ts: it re-reads the surface between steps, finds each offer by commandKind, stops at the FIRST refusal, and keeps the daemon's own {code, layer}. Tests cover: all four commands accepted; a mid-chain refusal stopping the chain with the exact code; and an absent offer reported as its own code (not a guessed version).

The 'Activate project' card renders in the v2 project setup board, lists each receipt as measured/missing with its reason, and exposes one button driving register -> bind_repository -> provider.probe -> project.activate. Its testids are pinned in a control-room test (parent DoD 3).
signingKeyRef is displayed as NOT a trust boundary in v0.1 with its reason - never rendered as a measured receipt (human decision 2026-09-04).
The card shows refusals VERBATIM as the daemon's `code @ layer`; a test asserts a refusal is rendered unparaphrased.

Gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`. A bare `pnpm test` is NOT evidence for an apps/** claim - the root vitest include has no apps/** (global rail 18).
taskRails: MIRROR policy-install-port.ts; do not invent a second dispatch idiom. Re-read the surface between steps - each commit moves the aggregate version and a cached offer is a stale version.
DO NOT ADD LINES TO apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts (422 lines, over the 400 cap). A new read gets its own module beside policy-read.ts / runs-read.ts.
The card spells NO witness, NO version and NO payload the daemon can state itself. Refusals are shown as the daemon's own code @ layer, never rewritten, and no credential value may reach the DOM.

implementationPlan.description: SCOPE NARROWED AT PLAN TIME — read this first. This row as filed carried the daemon read AND the v2 Activate card; enumerating the owned paths gave TWELVE (route + .js bridge + route test + read-dispatch + dev-proxy-paths + port + port test + screen + screen test + live-ops.tsx + cordum-app.tsx + shell-model.ts), over the 10 cap. The UI half is now task-3506e04abcef4fc3a69299ca238ae1b3 ('Activate project card: the browser drives the chain from one button'), which dependsOn THIS row. THIS ROW IS THE DAEMON READ ROUTE ONLY. DoD clauses 3, 4, 5 and 6 as written (the port, the card, its testids, the verbatim-refusal rendering) belong to that row and are NOT graded here — see the row comment recording the split. Then RE-MEASURE the route idiom: read `apps/daemon/src/http/policy-read.ts` (217 lines) end to end — it is the template for a dedicated read: a PATH const, a LAYER const, a frozen CODES array, view types, `authenticateHttpRequest` from http-command-ingress.js, and a capability check from daemon-command-vocabulary's CAPABILITIES. Confirm `apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts` is still 422 lines (`wc -l`) — it is over the 400 cap and must NOT be added to.

THE READ MODULE. Create `apps/daemon/src/http/activation-read.ts` exporting `ACTIVATION_READ_PATH = "/activation/read"`, a LAYER const, a frozen `ACTIVATION_READ_CODES` array (capability denied / project mismatch / unreadable, mirroring POLICY_READ_CODES' three-code shape), the receipt view types, and the request handler. The handler authenticates with `authenticateHttpRequest`, checks the capability, then calls child A's `measureActivationReceipts` and answers with each of the six members as measured/missing plus its `reason` string, and the signing entry marked NOT-measured. THIS ROUTE IS A READ: it measures and reports, and must NOT write the backup file or commit anything — if child A's measurement writes a backup as part of measuring, this route must call a read-only variant or the operator polls a card into writing a backup file every two seconds. Resolve that with child A's author and record the answer in a step note. Add the `.js` bridge sibling. Keep the module <=250 lines.

REGISTER THE ROUTE — all four touchpoints in `apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.ts`, which is the single file that owns them (measured: there is no separate read-dispatch test file at 68eb1c5d). (1) import `ACTIVATION_READ_PATH` and the handler beside the POLICY_READ_PATH import at :29; (2) add the path to the roster at :82-83 next to RUNS_READ_PATH and POLICY_READ_PATH; (3) add the non-POST method guard beside :439/:447; (4) add the dispatch branch beside :485/:489. Miss any one and the route either 404s or accepts a GET. Then add `"/activation/read"` to `apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts` (:7 and :25 list the existing read paths) so the dev server forwards it — without this the card works in production and silently fails in development, which is exactly where child C2 and the e2e lane will exercise it.

TESTS. Create `apps/daemon/src/http/activation-read.test.ts`. ARMS: (1) a fully measured project answers all six members measured, with the two hashes matching /^[0-9a-f]{64}$/; (2) ONE member unmeasurable is reported with its stable code AND layer from child A while the other five still read measured — per member, not a blanket failure; (3) NO SECRET LEAKS — drive the measurement with an env carrying a recognisable fake token and assert it appears nowhere in the serialised response body, `reason` strings included (this is the arm that matters most: the response is rendered straight onto an operator's screen); (4) an unauthenticated or under-capability request refuses with the route's own code at its own layer; (5) a non-POST method refuses, proving touchpoint 3 landed; (6) the signing entry is present and marked NOT-measured. Verify arms 2 and 4 go red by mutating the production surface — an arm that stays green when the code changes is not testing the code (global rail 1).

ROSTER SET-EQUALITY, BOTH DIRECTIONS. The read-route roster must be asserted bidirectionally (global rail 9): enumerate the paths the dispatcher ACTUALLY SERVES from the dispatch seam itself — not only from the roster constant — and assert set-equality with the declared roster. A test that iterates the roster constant alone can only see one direction: deleting a route shrinks its own iteration and stays green while a served path silently vanishes from the advertised surface. Do the same for the dev-proxy path list against the daemon's served read paths, so a route that exists in production but is not proxied in development is caught here rather than by a confused operator. If the existing suites carry no such assertion for the read routes, add it in this row — it is the guard that makes touchpoint 2 of the previous step meaningful.

GATES AND ADVERSARIAL REVIEW. Confirm every new production file is <=250 physical lines and that `affordance-read.ts` line count is UNCHANGED (`wc -l` before and after — proving nothing was added to the 422-line file). Run and QUOTE THE COUNT LINES: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` (dev-proxy-paths.ts is a control-room file), `pnpm typecheck`. Grade each leg on its `Test Files N passed` line, never its exit code — `pnpm --filter <pkg>` prints 'No projects matched the filters' and EXITS 0 for a non-package (global rail 8). Repo-wide legs are a path-attributed baseline (global rail 3): merge-base failures, HEAD failures, delta intersected with owned paths; disclose foreign red verbatim. ADVERSARIAL PASS: what does the route answer when the project has no store yet; when the measurement throws rather than returning `known:false` (it must become a coded refusal, not a 500 with a stack trace); when the card polls it every 2s (is anything written or spawned per poll — a `git rev-parse` per poll is acceptable, a backup file per poll is not); and when two reads race. Report every touched path in complete_step.modifiedFiles, including the .js bridge.

SCOPE NARROWED AT PLAN TIME (architect-d1711c47, 2026-09-04, measured at main 68eb1c5d) — READ BEFORE GRADING THIS ROW.

As filed, this row owned the daemon receipts read AND the v2 Activate card. Enumerating every consumer at plan time gave TWELVE owned paths:
activation-read.ts, activation-read.js, activation-read.test.ts, http-listener-read-dispatch.ts, dev-proxy-paths.ts, activation-port.ts, activation-port.test.ts, activation-screen.tsx, activation-screen.test.tsx, live-ops.tsx, cordum-app.tsx, shell-model.ts.

That is over the 10-file cap. The plan-time enumeration rail says a roster that breaches the cap is a SPLIT signal at plan time, not a discovery for the worker at step 5 — so the UI half was filed as:

**task-3506e04abcef4fc3a69299ca238ae1b3** — "Activate project card: the browser drives the chain from one button", dependsOn THIS row.

WHAT THIS ROW NOW OWNS: the daemon read route only — activation-read.ts + its .js bridge + its test, the four registration touchpoints in http-listener-read-dispatch.ts, and the dev-proxy path entry. Six paths, real headroom.

WHICH DoD CLAUSES MOVED. The `definitionOfDone` FIELD on this row is unamended and still reads as the combined row (I hold an architect id but `moe.set_task_dependencies` and the amendment tools refuse it — `[NOT_ALLOWED] architect or governor role required`). Grade this row against clauses 1, 2 and 7 only:
- CLAUSE 1 (dedicated read module, not affordance-read.ts; missing member reported with its stable code; no credential value in the body) — THIS ROW.
- CLAUSE 2 (route registered, .js bridge, bidirectional roster set-equality) — THIS ROW.
- CLAUSE 7 (gates with count lines) — THIS ROW.
- CLAUSE 3 (the activation port mirroring policy-install-port.ts) — MOVED to task-3506e04a.
- CLAUSE 4 (the card renders, one button drives the chain, testids pinned) — MOVED.
- CLAUSE 5 (signingKeyRef rendered as not-a-trust-boundary) — MOVED (the read still REPORTS it as not-measured; that part stays here).
- CLAUSE 6 (refusals rendered verbatim in the card) — MOVED.

TWO FINDINGS THE PLAN CARRIES, worth flagging separately:

1) THE READ MUST NOT WRITE. Child A's backup receipt COPIES the store file to `<project>/.moe-next/backups/<ts>.sqlite` and digests it. The card polls this read on a timer. If the route calls the full measurement, every poll writes a backup file. The plan makes resolving this (read-only measurement variant, or a cached last measurement) an explicit step with a recorded answer, rather than something discovered via a full backups directory.

2) THERE ARE FIVE REGISTRATION TOUCHPOINTS, NOT FOUR. Beyond the import, roster, method guard and dispatch branch in http-listener-read-dispatch.ts, `apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts` must list the new path. A route missing from that list works in production and silently 404s under the dev server — which is exactly where task-3506e04a and the e2e lane do their work.

MOUNT DECISION recorded for the UI row (owner-settled shape, architect-settled placement): the card mounts on the GOALS screen beside the blocked New Goal, not as a new nav id. `shell-model.ts:80-88` NAV_IDS has no 'setup' entry, and widening it would drag in its roster tests. `cr.activate.*` is free at 68eb1c5d (`cr.board.*` is taken).

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 6 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 10 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AT main 68eb1c5d.

THE ROUTE IDIOM (copy policy-read.ts, 217 lines): a `*_READ_PATH` const (policy-read.ts:27 `/policy/read`), a `LAYER` const (:28), a frozen `*_READ_CODES` array of three codes (:34-36), view interfaces, `authenticateHttpRequest` from ./http-command-ingress.js, `CAPABILITIES` from ../daemon-command-vocabulary.js. runs-read puts its path in a separate `runs-read-contract.ts` (:16) — either shape is acceptable.

THE FOUR REGISTRATION TOUCHPOINTS, all in apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.ts (there is NO separate read-dispatch test file — checked): import at :27/:29; path roster at :82-83; non-POST method guard at :439/:447; dispatch branch at :485/:489. All four are required; missing the guard means the route accepts a GET, missing the roster means it 404s.

THE DEV PROXY IS A FIFTH TOUCHPOINT AND IT IS EASY TO MISS: apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts:7 and :25 list `/affordances/read` and `/policy/read`. A route absent from that list works in production and silently fails under the dev server — which is where child C2 and the e2e lane run.

DO NOT TOUCH affordance-read.ts: 422 lines, over the 400 hard cap. Its `missingPrerequisites`-driven BLOCKED steps are how the card already learns which chain commands are blocked; the receipts read is additive, not a replacement.

CLIENT SIDE FOR REFERENCE (owned by C2, not here): apps/control-room/src/live/live-ops.ts:10 declares `POLICY_READ_PATH` as its own const and posts to it at :268 — the client re-declares the path rather than importing it across the app boundary.
planningNotes.risks:
1. THE READ MUST NOT WRITE. Child A's backup measurement COPIES the store file and digests it. If this route calls the full measurement, every poll of the card writes a backup into `<project>/.moe-next/backups/`. The card polls on a timer. Resolve this explicitly — a read-only measurement variant, or a cached last-measurement — and record the answer in a step note; do not leave it to be discovered by a full backups directory.

2. SECRET LEAK IS THE HIGHEST-CONSEQUENCE FAILURE HERE. This response is rendered directly onto an operator's screen and will appear in e2e screenshots. `providerCredentials` returns entries carrying a real token in `.value`; a reason string built by interpolating that object publishes it. The fake-token arm is not optional.

3. FIVE TOUCHPOINTS, NOT FOUR. The dev-proxy list is the one that fails silently and only in development — i.e. only where the next two rows do their work.

4. A ROSTER TEST THAT ITERATES ONLY THE CONSTANT IS VACUOUS. Enumerate the served set from the dispatch seam; otherwise deleting a route shrinks the test's own iteration and stays green (global rail 9).

5. A MEASUREMENT THAT THROWS MUST BECOME A CODED REFUSAL. An escaping exception is a 500 with a stack trace, which is both a leak and a fail-open in the operator's eyes.

6. This row's DoD clauses 3-6 as filed describe the port and the card, which now belong to task-3506e04abcef4fc3a69299ca238ae1b3. A grader reading the unamended DoD field will look for them here; the row comment and this note are the record that they moved.
